note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a BAN 9, PO 149 of 1972 4, 1926 Act 3, 6, 1978 Rules 3, 4; A06b BAN 9, PO 149 of 1972 4, 1926 Act 3, 6, 1978 Rules 3, 4; L05 BAN 14,  Bangladesh Citizenship (Temporary Provisions) Order 1972 2B): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: Generally applicable provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory unconditionally; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Bangladesh, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Bangladesh for 12 months immediately prior to the application, as well as during 4 out of 7 years predating the 12-month period, or the person has been ordinarily resident in Bangladesh for 5 years. Intent to reside in Bangladesh or to enter or continue in the service of Bangladesh required. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. ... The person acquiring a foreign citizenship (or is about to acquire) may relinquish Bangladeshi citizenship voluntarily, asking the government to release him. When Bangladeshi citizenship is not relinquished voluntarily in this situation, it lapses ipso facto. Except if person acquires the nationality of any state of Europe or North America or any other State specified by the Government in this behalf and applies for retention of his/her original nationality. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Bangladesh to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen other than by descent.; Person is born abroad to a citizen by descent (registration at a Bangladesh consulate required unless the citizen parent is in the service of Bangladesh at the time of the birth). ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Bangladesh. Unless born to a father who is a foreign diplomat and not a citizen of Bangladesh, or the father is an enemy alien and the child is born in a place then under occupation by the enemy. (Note: no practice is reported in this regard and Bangladesh does not apply the ius soli principle, but ius soli acquisition is arguably possible under BAN 4. In practice at least one of the parents must be a citizen.) ... No provision
